completion_rule: A row is DONE only with production reachability and its required focused, full-suite, fault/migration/resume, package, backend, platform, and no-silent-loss evidence. Omission is never completion.

note: The 57-row denominator survives. Historical benchmark execution and ground-truth scoring portions are deferred by current user scope; implementation, runtime, backend, resume, and handoff obligations remain active.
The canonical registry is the row-level authority. No row was fully complete at reconciliation.
These requirements supplement rather than replace the historical and canonical namespaces.

title: Complete supersession-aware corpus reconciliation
acceptance: Every relevant historical requirement is extracted with source identity, successor relation, implementation reachability, evidence, and remaining proof; the 127-file discovery denominator is reconciled without date-based supersession.

title: Clean package and installed-byte acceptance
acceptance: A clean checkout package builds, installs, verifies assets and runtime closure, upgrades, repairs, rolls back, and uninstalls without identity mismatch or dependence on a mutable installed tree.

title: Successful Codex end-to-end audit
acceptance: A fresh non-ground-truth Codex audit passes every required phase gate through final report on an exact packaged release candidate, with truthful degradation and route receipts.

title: Successful Claude end-to-end audit and resume
acceptance: A fresh non-ground-truth Claude audit completes through report and proves clean resume with no unauthorized relaunch or semantic mutation.

title: macOS installation and runtime portability
acceptance: A clean macOS machine can install, validate, start, stop, and resume Plamen using documented public commands while preserving cross-platform authority semantics.

title: Truthful dependency and compiler coverage
acceptance: Dependency research admission, source/build manifests, compiler resolution, vendored-library scoping, and degraded-run policy agree; unresolved imports or rejected research remain explicit debt.

title: Program Facts and static-analysis execution truth
acceptance: Supported Program Facts and static analyzers produce capability-scoped execution receipts and reachable consumer evidence; materialized filenames cannot impersonate tool execution.

title: Attention-repair global queue identity
acceptance: A confirmed repair uses ATT-N where N is the exact global queue row; validator accepts the canonical heading and rejects local renumbering and prefix collisions. Full-suite, package, and E2E proof remain required.

title: Sustainable cleanup-ledger retention
acceptance: Reference-aware, bounded retention preserves exact recovery semantics under concurrent readers/writers, crash, restart, path relocation, archive bounds, and both backend lifecycles.

title: Operational storage-capacity warning
acceptance: Bounded capacity and growth diagnostics are integrated into supported public operations without reading private contents or claiming safe deletion; package and cross-platform behavior are proven.

title: Typed startup failure diagnostics
acceptance: Startup preserves stable reason strings and digest-bound optional typed causes with bounded redaction and legacy replay compatibility; broader consumer and package validation remain required.

title: Worker lifecycle 24-case closure
acceptance: All 24 forensic lifecycle cases and the source's additional migration, binding, ownership, OS, and evidence requirements have production, fault, resume, and backend proof.

title: Bound captured-output storage
acceptance: Every native and model subprocess has a bounded spool or streaming backpressure policy; returned-tail truncation alone is insufficient.

title: Audit workspace hygiene and endpoint resilience
acceptance: Generated tests, fuzz harnesses, reports, transcripts, and tool outputs stay under owned output roots; load-bearing disappearance is detected; cleanup is bounded and recoverable; operator endpoint-protection guidance exists.

title: Single governed editable source
acceptance: Repository source is authoritative; installed trees are immutable products with reproducible receipts. Development changes cannot silently occur only in an installation or cache.

title: Backend routing final binding
acceptance: Every launch, retry, resume, provider-spool, completion, RunBundle, and evaluator projection consumes one exact typed route and records actual terminal provider/model evidence or explicit debt.

title: Resume, cancellation, timeout, and crash recovery
acceptance: Failures stop or recover without destructive reset, unauthorized new generation, lost debt, late write, duplicate authority, or false phase completion on both supported backends.

title: Portable development and operator documentation
acceptance: A clean-clone macOS or Windows user can install prerequisites, configure credentials outside the repository, run smoke tests, start/resume audits, diagnose storage, and continue this goal using repo-relative documentation.

title: Immutable validation evidence index
acceptance: Every acceptance claim binds exact source, package, command, environment capability, result, scope limits, and supersession; mutable prose is not the only receipt.

title: Private and evaluator boundary
acceptance: Credentials, target sources, findings, PoCs, scratchpads, ground truth, and neutral evaluator control remain outside the public tool tree; portable manifests disclose exclusions without private content.
